newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas Best aims to "fix" or sell losing units.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas Best aims to "fix" or sell losing units.

text.p: Arkansas Best Corp said Thursday it aims to "fix, sell or shut down" subsidiaries that posted losses in 1996.

And the company's board of directors has voted against reinstating dividends on its common stock amid a $0.56 per share loss for the fourth quarter ending December 31, versus a $1.41 loss for the same quarter last year, the company said.

"To return Arkansas Best to profitability, we will either fix, sell or shut down the operating subsidiaries which were not profitable in 1996," said Robert Young III, president and chief executive officer.
The poorly performing units helped elevate 1996 losses to $2.10 a share, a bit deeper than the $1.90 loss reported in 1995, the freight company reported in a prepared statement.
It said its less-than-truckload ("LTL") segment had a 1996 fourth quarter operating loss of $2.2 million compared with an operating loss of $31.2 million for the 1995 fourth quarter.
Arkansas Best said its tire operations segment was also a money loser, with an operating loss of $4.8 million for 1996 on revenues of $142 million.
The company paid a $0.01 per share dividend before suspending it during the second quarter of 1996, it said.
